cli.sessions_help.sessions: List active lop sessions and their resource usage; `sessions resume` reopens a set of stored sessions (paused/failed/all) in one bounded batch; `sessions cleanup` previews or runs the session cleanup policy; `sessions reclaim` previews or ends runtimes nothing can reach
cli.sessions_help.sessions_description: List active lop sessions and their resource usage; `sessions resume` reopens a set of stored sessions in one command; `sessions cleanup` previews or runs the session cleanup policy; `sessions reclaim` previews or ends runtimes nothing can reach.
cli.sessions_help.all: also list stored sessions that are not running (RSS/UPTIME/etc. are shown as — for these; sorted newest-first by last activity)
cli.sessions_help.limit: with --all (or a set filter), cap the stored rows listed; positive (default: 50)
cli.sessions_help.paused: list only stored sessions whose last turn was STOPPED rather than completed or lost — a deliberate stop or a build retirement (the set the bulk-resume path selects; implies --all)
cli.sessions_help.failed: list only stored sessions whose last recorded outcome was a failure (an involuntary death with no deliberate-stop evidence; implies --all). A death whose outcome was never imported is in neither set
cli.sessions_help.peer: list the sessions held by one peer device (its own catalogue, over the mesh)
cli.sessions_help.all_peers: also list the sessions other devices in this network are holding
cli.sessions_help.cleanup: Run the session cleanup policy now (use --dry-run to preview)
cli.sessions_help.cleanup_description: Apply session.cleanup.* from config (each limit overridable below) to the session store, in two classes: your conversations (needs session.cleanup.enabled: true unless --force) and delegated subagent/background sessions (session.cleanup.delegated.*, on by default). Every removal is recorded in <config>/sessions/.cleanup-log.jsonl.
cli.sessions_help.cleanup_dry_run: list what would be removed and why, without removing anything
cli.sessions_help.cleanup_force: run even when session.cleanup.enabled is false (lists first, then asks)
cli.sessions_help.cleanup_yes: do not ask for confirmation before removing
cli.sessions_help.cleanup_max_sessions: keep only the N most recently active sessions (overrides config)
cli.sessions_help.cleanup_max_inactive_d: remove sessions idle longer than N days (overrides config)
cli.sessions_help.cleanup_max_total_byte: trim the least recently active sessions past this store size (overrides config)
cli.sessions_help.cleanup_remove_empty: remove directories that never got a transcript (overrides config)
cli.sessions_help.cleanup_delegated_max_: remove subagent/background sessions idle over N hours, 2-720 (overrides config)
cli.sessions_help.reclaim: End session runtimes nothing can reach (dry run; --yes to act)
cli.sessions_help.reclaim_description: Find live session runtimes that no discovery record, no viewer, no attach and no existing config root can reach, and ask them to leave with SIGTERM. The runtime finishes any turn in flight first (its own signal drain, bounded by SIGNAL_DRAIN_S) — this command never sends SIGKILL. Any runtime with a record, an attached interface, a live root it does not own, or CPU spent inside the confirm window is refused.
cli.sessions_help.reclaim_dry_run: list what would be reclaimed, without signalling anything
cli.sessions_help.reclaim_yes: do not ask for confirmation before signalling
cli.sessions_help.reclaim_confirm_s: how long to watch before signalling (default: 60, minimum: 50). The window is the safety property: a runtime that gains a record, an attach or CPU inside it is dropped from the pass, and a window too short to measure CPU would drop one of the four refusals
cli.sessions_help.resume: Resume a set of stored sessions in one command (bulk)
cli.sessions_help.resume_description: Resume stored sessions without a shell loop: `--paused` (the interrupted/retired pair), `--failed` (error), or `--all` (every stored, non-live session — the widest reading, so given with the other selectors it wins). Newest first, capped at 20 unless --limit is given. Each session is reopened headlessly as `lop exec --resume <id> --background` with --message (default: a continuation). Children run with bounded concurrency (6 at a time) and print one line per session as it resolves. Exit codes: 0 = every selected session resumed; 1 = at least one failed or was unresolved at the bound; 2 = misuse (no set selected).
cli.sessions_help.resume_paused: select stored sessions whose last outcome was interrupted/retired (the 'Unseen interruption' pair; implies the store scope)
cli.sessions_help.resume_failed: select stored sessions whose last outcome was error (implies the store scope)
cli.sessions_help.resume_all: select every stored, non-live session (newest first, capped); the widest reading — given with --paused/--failed it wins
cli.sessions_help.resume_dry_run: print the selected set (newest first) and resume nothing
cli.sessions_help.resume_limit: cap the set at the N newest matches (default: 20)
cli.sessions_help.resume_message: the message each resumed session runs (default: a continuation — 'Continue the task from where it left off.')
cli.sessions_help.move: Move a conversation to another device, or bring one home
cli.sessions_help.move_description: Hand a conversation to another device (`--to build-box`), or bring one that lives elsewhere back here (`--to local`). The conversation keeps its id and the copy on the device it left is deleted, unless `--keep` is given, which leaves the original running and mints a NEW id for the copy. A session with a turn in flight is refused, not interrupted.
cli.sessions_help.move_session: the conversation id to move (with --cancel-queued, the id is that flag's value)
cli.sessions_help.move_to: a peer device (id or name), or `local` to bring the conversation here
cli.sessions_help.move_keep: copy and leave the original running; the copy gets a new id and a fork marker
cli.sessions_help.move_wait: re-check a busy conversation every 5s, up to SECONDS (bare: up to 30 min)
cli.sessions_help.move_queue: wait for the next safe point instead of refusing a busy conversation: the move is queued durably on the conversation's device and runs when its turn ends (attached clients there are announced and given a window to follow or detach). Ignored with --keep
cli.sessions_help.move_cancel_queued: cancel a queued move that has not started yet; takes the conversation id and nothing else
cli.sessions_help.move_from_replica: recover the last copy this device synced as a NEW session, for when the device that held it is gone
cli.sessions_help.move_engage_on_arrival: start the conversation on the destination as soon as it lands, so it is live there without a first prompt; a conversation whose turn is in flight is still refused rather than drained, and a failure to start it does not affect the move — so the exit status is the MOVE's: a script reads `engagement.engaged` in --json, and on a move to a peer that device's own log is where the outcome shows
cli.sessions_help.sync: Pull a copy of a conversation another device owns
cli.sessions_help.sync_description: Bring this device's copy of a conversation it does not own up to date. The copy is stored outside the session store and is never opened as a session; `lop sessions move <id> --to local --from-replica` recovers it as a new one.
cli.sessions_help.sync_owner: the peer that holds it (default: ask)
